doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: First recording with Milt Hinton and Carmen Cavallaro
summary: His first record, aged 18 in 1961, for Decca with Cavallaro, guided by Milt Hinton; Rowe takes his birth date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah. Milt Hinton too. Guys like that.
Milt Hinton. My first recording he was on.

Yeah. I was with Carmen Cavallaro for a year, at 18, and hanging on by the skin of my teeth you know. Because it was demanding. It wasn’t a real jazz gig but it was like he carried a quartet. I mean piano, bass, drums and guitar. He carried three other musicians beside himself. And he had a show and he played very flashy kind of piano but tempos and styles and I had to come up with that stuff. And so I was with him maybe six months and we were in New York, he lived in New York and we used to spend a lot of time there. And he was recording for Decca. And he had a record date and I was going to be on it and the guitarist who was also a New Yorker but he wasn’t going to use the bass © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

player, he was in between bass players, so I showed up at this studio and they delivered the bass and I look and the tag said Milt Hinton. I went oh my God. I was scared to death anyway. I was just petrified you know. But Milt Hinton, and he came in and just guided me right through it. He was like Benny Carter. This real classy guy and he knew what he was dealing with. He had this 18-year-old frightened kid and I just kept my eye on him and he just guided me right through it. And so that’s my first record.
That’s a great story. This would have been sixty what?
Oh yeah. I have to get your date of birth by the way, for my records.
Absolutely, just unclip yourself. Tim we’re taking a little pause here. What is your date of birth, I’ll just write it down.
